instruction: Add the text "A Beautiful Day" to the content area of the first slide and make it bold.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully inserted title 'Happy Family' on slide 1 and changed font to Microsoft JhengHei. Used terminal to verify font availability, then typed text and set font in LibreOffice Impress.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click on title placeholder, type text, change font via font selector, use terminal for font verification, navigate LibreOffice Impress UI
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different placeholder (content area instead of title) and a different formatting property (bold instead of font family). The agent proved it can interact with text areas and apply formatting.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding text to the content/body placeholder on slide 1 and making it bold. Getter extracts text and bold property from the OBJECT placeholder (type 7). Metric gives 0.5 for correct text and 0.5 for bold formatting.

scoring_breakdown.content_text: 0.5 - Correct text 'A Beautiful Day' in content area

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements (text content and bold formatting) are verified with appropriate partial credit (0.5 each)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_text') and expected.get('expected_bold')
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state
Getter reads placeholder type 7 (OBJECT) which is a reasonable assumption for the content area, though layout-dependent
Minor concern: getter iterates all runs and overwrites is_bold, so only the last run's bold value is checked; acceptable for typical single-run bold text scenarios
Minor concern: run.font.bold returns None for inherited bold, but metric correctly handles this with 'actual_bold is not None' check
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking bold across all runs (e.g., all(run.font.bold for run in para.runs)) to handle multi-run text more robustly
Consider adding fallback placeholder types (e.g., type 1 BODY, type 15 BODY) in case the content area uses a different placeholder type in the slide layout
